entries.subject: Math
entries.title: Quadratic formula
entries.content: For ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0, x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / (2a). The discriminant D = b² - 4ac: D > 0 gives two distinct real roots, D = 0 one repeated real root, and D < 0 no real roots over the real numbers.

entries.subject: Math
entries.title: Pythagorean theorem
entries.content: In a right triangle with legs a and b and hypotenuse c: a² + b² = c².

entries.subject: Math
entries.title: Circle formulas
entries.content: Area A = πr². Circumference C = 2πr = πd, where r is radius and d = 2r is diameter.

entries.subject: Math
entries.title: Triangle area
entries.content: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × perpendicular height.

entries.subject: Math
entries.title: Percentage
entries.content: Percentage = (part / whole) × 100%. To find p% of a number N, compute (p/100) × N.

entries.subject: Math
entries.title: Simple interest
entries.content: Simple interest SI = (P × R × T) / 100 when R is percent per time period and T uses the same time unit. Amount = P + SI.

entries.subject: Math
entries.title: Speed-distance-time
entries.content: Speed = distance/time; distance = speed × time; time = distance/speed. Keep units consistent.

entries.subject: Math
entries.title: Arithmetic mean
entries.content: Arithmetic mean = sum of all observations / number of observations.

entries.subject: Math
entries.title: Exponent laws
entries.content: For suitable nonzero bases: a^m × a^n = a^(m+n); a^m/a^n = a^(m-n); (a^m)^n = a^(mn); a^0 = 1 for a ≠ 0; a^(-n) = 1/a^n.

entries.subject: Science
entries.title: Newton's laws
entries.content: First law: an object remains at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless acted on by a net external force. Second law: net force equals rate of change of momentum; for constant mass, F = ma. Third law: interacting bodies exert equal-magnitude, opposite-direction forces on each other.

entries.subject: Science
entries.title: Weight
entries.content: Weight is gravitational force: W = mg, where m is mass and g is gravitational field strength/acceleration due to gravity.

entries.subject: Science
entries.title: Density
entries.content: Density ρ = mass/volume. SI unit: kg/m³.

entries.subject: Science
entries.title: Work
entries.content: For a constant force, work W = F s cosθ, where θ is the angle between force and displacement. If force is along displacement, W = Fs.

entries.subject: Science
entries.title: Power
entries.content: Average power P = work/time = energy transferred/time. SI unit: watt (W), equal to joule per second.

entries.subject: Science
entries.title: Mechanical energy
entries.content: Translational kinetic energy KE = ½mv². Near Earth's surface, gravitational potential energy change can be written ΔPE = mgΔh.

entries.subject: Science
entries.title: Ohm's law
entries.content: For an ohmic conductor under constant physical conditions, V = IR. Electrical power can be written P = VI; using Ohm's law, P = I²R or V²/R.

entries.subject: Science
entries.title: Wave speed
entries.content: Wave speed v = fλ, where f is frequency and λ is wavelength.

entries.subject: Science
entries.title: Photosynthesis
entries.content: A common summary is: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂, using light energy. The full biological process is more complex than this net equation.

entries.subject: Science
entries.title: Aerobic cellular respiration
entries.content: A common net summary is C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O, with released energy captured in forms including ATP.

entries.subject: Science
entries.title: Atomic structure
entries.content: Atoms contain a nucleus with protons and neutrons, with electrons occupying quantum states around the nucleus. Atomic number equals the number of protons.

entries.subject: Science
entries.title: pH
entries.content: For dilute aqueous solutions, pH = -log₁₀(a_H+), often approximated using hydrogen-ion concentration. At 25°C, pH 7 is neutral; values below 7 are acidic and above 7 basic, though the exact neutral pH depends on temperature.

entries.subject: Science
entries.title: Conservation of mass
entries.content: In a closed system during an ordinary chemical reaction, total mass is conserved: atoms are rearranged rather than created or destroyed.
